posts.title: How to Scale and Accelerate Distributed Digital Ising Machines
posts.subtitle: A calibrated performance model and a systematic framework for system-level acceleration
posts.author: Tong Wu et al. · CMU · Pitt · UCSB
posts.tldr: Large Ising problems outgrow one device and expose three system costs: coupling data moving through the memory hierarchy, colored Gibbs updates synchronising, and boundary states crossing device links. We separate these costs in a performance model calibrated across GPUs, FPGAs, and ASICs. Roofline analysis shows Ising workloads have low arithmetic intensity, and measurements show performance drops sharply once the working set spills beyond on-chip storage. We develop two systematic approaches to system-level acceleration: bounded-staleness sampling reduces synchronisation frequency, and a phase-offset pipeline places boundary exchange behind interior computation. A fabricated multi-chip ASIC implements the streaming schedule.
